name: Cooley

attributes.attribute: setting of the Táin Bó Cuailnge climax
Irish form of the name Cooley

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cooley is a peninsula in the north-east of County Louth in Ireland, between Dundalk Bay and the waters of Carlingford Lough. Cuailnge is the Irish form of the name. Many of the climactic scenes of the Irish epic Táin Bó Cuailnge, the Cattle Raid of Cooley, play out on this ground. The name also points readers to the fuller account under Cuailnge.

okr.objective: Give the geography of Cooley and its place in the Táin.
key_results: Locate the peninsula between Dundalk Bay and Carlingford Lough.
Give the Irish form Cuailnge of the name.
Tie the peninsula to the climax of the Cattle Raid of Cooley.
